legend.0: Breaks accepted visible, manual, heartbeat, or process protocol behavior.
legend.1: Preserves few observable contracts and leaves major behavior gaps.
legend.2: Preserves several observable contracts but leaves material behavior gaps.
legend.3: Preserves the observable contracts with bounded untested edge cases.
legend.4: Preserves all observable, manual, log, and protocol contracts with no unresolved behavior change.

legend.0: Requires a broad redesign, new framework, or many unrelated moving parts.
legend.1: Requires several new subsystems and difficult coordination.
legend.2: Requires a moderate focused change with material coordination.
legend.3: Requires focused changes with bounded coordination.
legend.4: Requires the smallest coherent endpoint change.

legend.0: Needs fragile bootstrap, broad dependency distribution, or changed output paths.
legend.1: Has major bootstrap, dependency, or distribution risk.
legend.2: Has a workable build with several unresolved bootstrap decisions.
legend.3: Uses approved paths and a bounded build with minor decisions.
legend.4: Uses a simple reproducible build and distribution sequence.

legend.0: Cannot isolate regressions or restore the accepted baseline.
legend.1: Needs broad new tests before useful rollback is possible.
legend.2: Supports partial isolation and rollback with material untested areas.
legend.3: Supports staged tests, evidence, and rollback for known contracts.
legend.4: Supports small isolated tests, direct comparison, and rollback at each slice.

legend.0: Creates high long-term duplication or framework burden.
legend.1: Creates substantial ongoing maintenance across runtime and tooling.
legend.2: Creates moderate burden or duplicated contracts.
legend.3: Keeps ongoing maintenance bounded with limited duplication.
legend.4: Minimizes code, dependency, and contract maintenance.
